cards.back: Document defining the authority, scope, responsibilities, and recipients of an audit engagement.
Examining a representative sample of a control.
Verifiable statement submitted to audit, e.g., "this control has been enforced since January."
Comparison between current state and a target framework to identify gaps.
Self-assessment = evaluation by the team; independent third-party audit = externalized, defensible assurance.
Comparing the organization's practices against industry peers or an external framework.
Levels of information provided to the tester: all, none, or part of the system.
Offensive = attacking; defensive = verifying detection/response; integrated = collaborative work (purple team).
Collection without contacting the target: public sources, no logs generated on the victim.
Direct interaction (scans, queries): leaves traces and must be authorized by the ROE.
Authorized testing of physical controls: locks, badges, mantraps, tailgating.
Reconnaissance, weaponization, delivery, exploitation, installation, command and control, actions on objectives.
Matrix of adversary tactics and techniques. Enterprise has 14 tactics (not 11).
Adversary, victim, capability, infrastructure — with time and context metadata.
Kill Chain = progression phases; ATT&CK = techniques organized by tactic.
Sectoral, international, or region-specific frameworks used as audit targets.
Functional = does the feature do what is expected? Behavioral = does the system behave as expected in a scenario?
